ChrgBr.name: Charge Bearer
ChrgBr.note: Who pays the transaction charges. A mismatch between what the debtor agreed and what the message says is a leading cause of unexpected deductions and repair fees.

codes.DEBT: Borne by debtor — all charges are paid by the sender, creditor receives the full amount
codes.CRED: Borne by creditor — charges are deducted from the transferred amount
codes.SHAR: Shared — sender pays its own bank's charges, creditor pays the rest
codes.SLEV: Following service level — charges follow the rules of the scheme named in Service Level (used by SEPA)

SttlmMtd.name: Settlement Method
SttlmMtd.note: How the interbank leg actually settles. Determines which other elements of Settlement Information are allowed.

codes.INDA: Instructed agent — settled on an account the instructed agent services (nostro held by the instructing agent)
codes.INGA: Instructing agent — settled on an account the instructing agent services (vostro)
codes.COVE: Cover — settled by a separate cover payment, typically a pacs.009 COV
codes.CLRG: Clearing system — settled through a payment clearing or RTGS system

PmtMtd.name: Payment Method
PmtMtd.note: Set once per payment information block in pain.001. Direct debit initiation (pain.008) uses PaymentMethod2Code, where the only value is DD.

codes.TRA: Credit transfer governed by a specific agreement or convention

SeqTp.name: Sequence Type
SeqTp.note: Where a direct debit collection sits in the life of its mandate. SEPA sequencing errors (sending RCUR before any FRST) are a common rejection cause.

codes.FRST: First collection under a recurring mandate
codes.FNAL: The final collection under a mandate
codes.OOFF: One-off collection — the mandate authorises a single collection only
codes.RPRE: Re-presented collection, following an earlier failure

CdtDbtInd.name: Credit / Debit Indicator
CdtDbtInd.note: Direction of an amount, balance or entry. In statements, always read an amount together with this indicator — ISO 20022 amounts are unsigned.

codes.DBIT: Debit — money out of the account

Prty.name: Priority
Prty.note: A processing-order hint, not a settlement guarantee. Most schemes override or ignore it; use Service Level for anything binding.

ClrChanl.name: Clearing Channel
ClrChanl.note: Which class of clearing infrastructure should carry the payment.

codes.BOOK: Settled internally on the agent's own books, no external system

SvcLvl.name: Service Level
SvcLvl.note: The rulebook the payment is executed under. This is the element that binds a payment to a scheme, so it is usually the first thing a scheme's validation checks.

codes.SEPA: Single Euro Payments Area scheme rules
codes.INST: Instant — immediate 24/7 execution (SCT Inst, NPP, FedNow style)
codes.BKTR: Bank transfer, settled between the agents directly

LclInstrm.name: Local Instrument
LclInstrm.note: Scheme-defined product or instrument within a service level. Unlike most codelists this one is genuinely local — the same code can mean different things in different schemes, and many schemes publish their own values in a proprietary sub-element instead. Always read it against the specific rulebook.

codes.CORE: SEPA core direct debit — consumer scheme, full refund rights
codes.COR1: SEPA core direct debit with a shortened settlement cycle (withdrawn in most markets)
codes.B2B: SEPA business-to-business direct debit — no refund right, debtor must be a business
codes.RTGS: Payment to be cleared through an RTGS system

CtgyPurp.name: Category Purpose
CtgyPurp.note: Why the payment is being made, at a level the *agents* act on — it can change routing, cut-off or clearing treatment. Distinct from Purpose, which is for the creditor's benefit and should not drive processing.

codes.CORT: Settlement of a trade (trade or treasury operation)
codes.SALA: Salary payment — often routed as a bulk file and may be privacy-restricted

Purp.name: Purpose
Purp.note: The underlying reason for the payment, carried unaltered end to end for the creditor's reconciliation. Agents must not use it for routing decisions — that is Category Purpose's job. Several hundred values exist; the common ones are below.

TxSts.name: Transaction / Group Status
TxSts.note: Reported in pain.002 and pacs.002 at group, payment-information and transaction level. The critical distinction is accepted-for-processing (ACTC/ACSP) versus actually settled (ACSC/ACCC) — treating ACSP as final is a classic reconciliation bug.

codes.ACTC: Accepted technical validation — syntax and schema are valid, nothing more
codes.ACCP: Accepted customer profile — passed profile and format checks
codes.ACSP: Accepted settlement in process — in the clearing flow, not yet settled
codes.ACSC: Accepted settlement completed at the debtor's agent — the debit has settled
codes.ACCC: Accepted settlement completed at the creditor's agent — funds credited
codes.ACWC: Accepted with change — processed, but the agent altered something (truncated or repaired data)
codes.ACWP: Accepted without posting — accepted, but not yet booked to the creditor account
codes.ACFC: Accepted funds checked — accepted and funds confirmed available
codes.PDNG: Pending — held awaiting something; a reason code should say what
codes.RCVD: Received — logged at the receiving agent, validation not started
codes.PART: Partially accepted — some transactions in the group accepted, others rejected
codes.PATC: Partially accepted technical correct — awaiting further authorisations
codes.RJCT: Rejected — will not be processed; a reason code is mandatory in practice

StsRsn.name: Status Reason
StsRsn.note: Why a payment was rejected or is pending. Returned in pain.002 and pacs.002. The AC/AG/AM/BE families are worth memorising — they account for most real-world rejections.

codes.AC01: Incorrect account number — format or checksum invalid
codes.AC06: Account blocked for this type of transaction
codes.AG01: Transaction forbidden on this account type
codes.AM02: Amount exceeds the agreed maximum for this transaction type
codes.AM09: Wrong amount — not the amount that was agreed
codes.BE01: Debtor or creditor name does not match the account
codes.DT01: Invalid date — requested execution date is not a valid business date
codes.MS02: Refused by the customer, no reason given
codes.MS03: Refused by the agent, no reason given
codes.RC01: Invalid bank identifier — BIC or clearing code unknown
codes.RR01: Missing debtor account or identification — regulatory requirement
codes.RR02: Missing debtor name or address — regulatory requirement
codes.RR03: Missing creditor name or address — regulatory requirement
codes.SL01: Blocked by a service level agreement or standing instruction
codes.NARR: Reason supplied as free text in Additional Information

RtrRsn.name: Return Reason
RtrRsn.note: Why a settled payment is being sent back via pacs.004. A return is a new payment in the opposite direction, not a cancellation — the original stays settled, which matters for reconciliation and for charges already taken.

codes.ARDT: Already returned — the transaction has previously been returned
codes.BE01: Name and account do not match
codes.MD06: Returned by the debtor, disputing an authorised collection

CxlRsn.name: Cancellation Reason
CxlRsn.note: Why camt.056 is asking for a payment to be recalled. FRAD and TECH usually get priority handling; CUST is a best-efforts request the receiving agent may refuse.

codes.AGNT: Requested by an agent in the chain
codes.CUTA: Cancelled to enable a technical repair and re-send
codes.UPAY: Undue payment — should not have been made

InvstgtnSts.name: Investigation Execution Confirmation
InvstgtnSts.note: The answer camt.029 gives to a camt.056 cancellation request. Note that CNCL means the money was actually recalled, while ACVA only acknowledges the request — do not treat them as equivalent.

codes.CNCL: Cancelled — the payment was successfully recalled
codes.PDCR: Pending cancellation — accepted and in progress
codes.RJCR: Rejected cancellation — the agent will not recall the payment
codes.ACVA: Accepted valid — the request is valid and under investigation
codes.ACNR: Accepted, no reason for the request was provided
codes.MODI: Modified as requested instead of cancelled
codes.IPAY: Payment had already been made before the request arrived

RvslRsn.name: Reversal Reason
RvslRsn.note: Why an initiating party is reversing its own instruction in pain.007. Only the originator can reverse; a debtor disputing a collection goes through a return or refund instead.

codes.MD02: Mandate details are missing or incorrect
codes.MD06: Disputed by the debtor as unauthorised
codes.MS02: Refused by the customer, no reason given
codes.MS03: Refused by the agent, no reason given

BalTp.name: Balance Type
BalTp.note: Which balance a camt.052/053 figure represents. OPBD and CLBD are the booked bookends that must reconcile against the entries; CLAV is what the customer can actually spend. Confusing booked with available balance is the most common statement-parsing error.

codes.OPBD: Opening booked — booked balance at the start of the period
codes.CLBD: Closing booked — booked balance at the end of the period
codes.PRCD: Previously closed booked — the prior statement's closing balance
codes.CLAV: Closing available — funds actually available after holds and float
codes.FWAV: Forward available — availability on a future date

RmtLctnMtd.name: Remittance Location Method
RmtLctnMtd.note: How remittance detail that is too large for the payment message is delivered separately — the pointer that links a payment to a remt.001.

codes.URID: Uniform resource identifier — a link to the detail

AdrTp.name: Address Type
AdrTp.note: Qualifies a postal address. Relevant to the structured-address migration: schemes increasingly reject PBOX for the debtor and require a real street address.

ClrSysId.name: Clearing System Identification
ClrSysId.note: Names the domestic clearing system whose member identifier appears in Member Identification. This is how a national sort code or routing number travels inside an ISO 20022 message.

codes.USABA: United States — ABA routing transit number
